mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the GDP growth rate (GDPC1) over the past four quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which historically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines by less than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% over three consecutive months signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 7.0% and S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 100 over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which historically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by less than 5% quarter-over-quarter and S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary cycle, which increases discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 5.0% and S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

failure_condition: If RSAFS declines by less than $50 billion quarter-over-quarter and S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
